source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF project URL, OpenReview record, README title/authors, and gh repository metadata directly identify isaac7778/FIRE. The automatic source-inventory row says repository_without_visual_source, but current gh tree inspection found matching rendered assets for Figures 2, 3, 4(a), and 4(b). No paper TeX, plot/figure/table generator, notebook, data export, or style file was found; assets/iclr2026fire.png is a related README screenshot and is not treated as the vector Figure 1 source. paper_style.palette_strategy: FIRE is consistently red in principal comparisons; vision adds yellow/orange/pink/purple/green/teal/blue/gray method colors, while reference lines are black/gray dashed. The categorical palette is expressive but not reliably grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 1 is primarily vector PDF diagram geometry/text; Figures 2–8 are embedded raster composite plots; Tables 1–10 are native text/vector tables. The PDF raster XObjects are high resolution, but plot-generating source and data are not public in the inspected repository.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern manuscript, caption and table typography is consistent. Raster plots share white backgrounds, light gray grids and compact sans-serif labels, but legends and method palettes are local; appendix tables are configuration inventories rather than result tables.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Illustration of FIRE. Solving a constrained optimization problem, FIRE places weights at the intersection of high-stability and high-plasticity manifolds.

color.semantic_mapping: FIRE and full-reset paths, manifold fills, weight points, and text use separate pastel/red/gray roles.

encodings.x: Conceptual movement from learned weights toward a reset or constrained intersection
encodings.y: Conceptual placement inside high-stability and high-plasticity manifolds
encodings.line: Colored FIRE path versus neutral full-reset path and arrow direction
encodings.text: Direct labels for W, W0, W~, High Stability, and High Plasticity

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual method interface rather than a quantitative sample. It illustrates the constrained minimum-SFE/zero-DfI target and has no observations, denominator, error or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: The introduction frames stability and plasticity as competing properties; Figure 1 turns the constrained formulation into a visual intersection. Sections 3.1–3.4 and the polar/Procrustes derivation formalize the operation, while Figures 2–5 test behavior and proxies.
design_strengths: The intersection of stability and plasticity is immediately legible without axes.
Direct labels and a small local legend keep the process readable in a single-column footprint.
design_weaknesses: Manifold membership and W~ depend on surrounding notation.
Pastel fills and red/gray paths are not robust in grayscale or for color-vision-deficient reproduction.
The local diagram language differs from the raster result plots, and no empirical scale is shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use one conceptual geometry panel to connect an optimization constraint to competing properties; duplicate color roles with shape or line semantics when the diagram will be printed.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Continual visual learning results. Warm-start setting (a): training begins with only 10% of the data before continuing on the full dataset. Continual setting (b): the dataset is revealed in ten stages, expanding from 10% to 100% in 10% increments. Class-incremental setting (c): new classes are introduced over 20 phases, with an equal number of classes added at each phase.

color.semantic_mapping: Method colors identify FIRE, Shrink Perturb, CBP, SNR, Muon, Full reset, Parseval, DASH, ReDo, L2init, and Base.

encodings.line: Method trajectories and dashed horizontal reference lines
encodings.text: Row labels, panel titles, legend, reference labels, and a continual-learning zoom inset

figures.data_and_statistics: CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, CIFAR-100/ViT-Tiny, and Tiny ImageNet/VGG-16 are shown under warm-start, ten-stage continual, and 20-phase class-incremental protocols. Appendix E.1 reports three seeds, but the ribbon center and dispersion semantics are not defined; exact endpoints and tests are absent.
figures.evidence_relation: Sections 4.1 and the visual-learning results claim recovery across three data-arrival protocols; Figure 2 is the principal behavior evidence. Tables 2 and 7–9 document settings and selected values, and Figure 8 supplies train-accuracy counterparts. The public vision README explicitly maps vision/fig2.png to Fig. 2.
design_strengths: Protocol rows make three data-arrival regimes comparable.
Shared axes and a common legend support cross-panel scanning; the row-(b) zoom inset preserves a dense transition.
design_weaknesses: Eight panels and eleven methods are crowded, with neighboring hues that are not grayscale-safe.
Ribbons are undefined and the caption states setup rather than the observed ordering.
Curve separation must be estimated because no exact endpoint/result table accompanies the figure.
figures.reusable_pattern: Align small multiples by protocol and dataset with shared axes and a common method legend; reserve an inset for a dense transition and define band semantics next to the figure.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Continual pretraining of GPT-0.1B. Models are first pretrained on WikiText-103 and then continually trained on a new dataset consisting of a mixture of OpenWebText and WikiText-103. From left to right, results correspond to models initialized from the best checkpoint during pretraining, from 30k pretraining iterations, and from 60k pretraining iterations.

color.semantic_mapping: FIRE, Shrink Perturb, Full Reset, Base, and translucent band fills are separated by local method color.

encodings.facet: Initialization checkpoint: best, 30k, or 60k pretraining iterations
encodings.text: Panel titles, shared legend, and axis labels

figures.data_and_statistics: GPT-0.1B is first pretrained on WikiText-103 and then continued on OpenWebText plus WikiText-103 from best, 30k, and 60k checkpoints. Appendix E.2 reports three seeds, but the ribbon statistic is unspecified and no exact endpoint or test is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 4.2 uses the three checkpoint facets to test FIRE under different LLM starting points. Table 3 gives common LLM settings and Table 10 gives checkpoint-specific values; language/README.md explicitly maps language/fig3.png to Fig. 3.
design_strengths: Checkpoint facets isolate initialization sensitivity in one compact comparison surface.
A shared loss axis and legend make the three starting conditions easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: The caption is setup-heavy and does not state the observed ordering.
Uncertainty bands are undefined and curves become hard to distinguish near convergence.
No numeric endpoint table accompanies the visual.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use checkpoint facets to turn initialization sensitivity into one comparison surface, paired with an endpoint table and explicit seed/band definition.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Reinforcement learning results. Discrete control with DQN on three Atari environments that suffer from severe plasticity loss (a) and continuous control with SAC on three HumanoidBench tasks (b). The black dashed line indicates the point at which reinitialization is applied.

color.semantic_mapping: Within each DQN/SAC row, FIRE, Shrink Perturb, Plasticity Injection, Reset, and untreated control are keyed by local legend color.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: one shared legend per control row

encodings.line: Return trajectory and dashed midpoint intervention marker
encodings.text: Task titles, row legends, axis labels, and midpoint line

figures.data_and_statistics: DQN covers Asterix-v4, BeamRider-v4, and DemonAttack-v4; SAC/SimBa covers h1-walk-v0, h1-balance_simple-v0, and h1-run-v0. One midpoint intervention uses the same checkpoint/replay conditions. Appendix E.3 reports five seeds, but ribbon aggregation, failure handling and exact returns are unspecified.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 4.3 claims recovery across discrete and continuous control; Figure 4 is the cross-domain behavior evidence. Tables 4–5 specify ALE/DQN and HumanoidBench/SimBa settings. rl/dqn/README.md and rl/sac/README.md explicitly identify the matching rendered assets; the DQN README notes a vectorized four-environment reproduction difference.
design_strengths: The vertical intervention line aligns the causal event across all tasks.
Row-wise legends avoid one ten-item legend, and task facets expose both favorable and difficult trajectories.
design_weaknesses: Local palettes force method-color relearning and are not grayscale-safe.
The dashed intervention line can be confused with a trajectory; bands and five-seed aggregation are undefined.
No exact recovery value or failure rate is tabulated.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned task facets and one shared intervention marker to compare post-event trajectories across control families; define event, band, seed, and failure semantics in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: Ablation study results. Final performance of FIRE with varying numbers of iterations for Netwon-Schulz algorithm (a). Comparison of FIRE and baselines in terms of loss curvature (maximum eigenvalue of the Hessian), plasticity (DfI), and stability (normalized SFE) (b).

color.semantic_mapping: FIRE, Shrink Perturb, DASH, full-reset/warm-start references, and pale error-bar fills distinguish iteration and proxy comparisons.

encodings.x: NS iteration count in row (a); method in row (b)
encodings.y: Final test accuracy, maximum Hessian eigenvalue, DfI, or normalized SFE
encodings.shape: Point-line in row (a), rectangular bars in row (b)
encodings.line: Iteration trend and dashed reference lines
encodings.text: Panel titles, metric labels, reference labels, and method ticks

figures.data_and_statistics: Row (a) covers three vision tasks at 5, 10, 20, 30, and 40 Newton–Schulz iterations. Row (b) compares FIRE, Shrink Perturb, and DASH: rendered values are approximately curvature 9/10/0, DfI 50/180/900, and normalized SFE 0.58/0.65/0.70, with full-reset SFE at 1. Error-bar semantics and aggregation are not defined, so these are visual estimates.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 4.4 and the theory connect SFE/DfI to stability/plasticity; Figure 5 is the main mechanism/iteration check. Figure 6 expands iteration dynamics and Figure 7 tests coefficients, while Figures 2–4 show downstream behavior. No public plot source or exact data table was found.
design_strengths: The figure combines a practical iteration choice with theory-facing proxies.
The full-reset SFE reference makes the normalization interpretable, and separate metric facets avoid collapsing mechanisms.
design_weaknesses: The error bars lack a definition and exact bar values are unavailable.
Rows use different x semantics, the caption contains the “Netwon-Schulz” typo, and missing aggregation details weaken reproduction.
figures.reusable_pattern: Put iteration choice beside mechanism proxies and a common reference baseline, with exact values and uncertainty definitions in a companion table.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6: Effect of number of FIRE iterations. Test accuracy of FIRE with single iteration and 10 iterations (left). Change of SFE during FIRE iterations (middle). Change of DfI during FIRE iterations (right).

color.semantic_mapping: Iteration-10, iteration-1, Base, and diagnostic trajectories use local blue/orange/green/black roles.

encodings.x: Epoch in accuracy panel; FIRE iteration in diagnostic panels
encodings.text: Panel titles, left legend, axes, and log tick notation on DfI

figures.data_and_statistics: The left panel shows Tiny ImageNet/VGG-16 accuracy for one versus ten FIRE iterations and Base; middle and right panels show SFE and DfI over iterations 0–20. DfI is displayed on a logarithmic y-axis while the middle diagnostic is linear-looking. No exact endpoints, seeds, aggregation or uncertainty are given.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 5’s iteration ablation is expanded into diagnostic trajectories, showing the proxy changes used to motivate a small iteration count. It is descriptive appendix evidence rather than a new benchmark estimand.
design_strengths: Behavior and two mechanism diagnostics share the iteration storyline.
The log DfI axis exposes its large dynamic range.
design_weaknesses: Mixed panel y scales are not called out in the caption.
No bands or run information are given, and the middle/right panels lack independent legends or direct curve labels.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair an outcome curve with proxy trajectories across intervention iterations, explicitly label panel-specific scales and report the stopping choice numerically.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: Effect of Newton Schulz iteration coefficients on FIRE. FIRE and FIRE with Muon’s coefficients are evaluated on warm-start setting under CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 (left), CIFAR-100 with ViT-Tiny (middle), and Tiny ImageNet with VGG-16 (right).

color.semantic_mapping: Standard FIRE coefficients, Muon coefficients, and gray/black warm-start/full-reset references are separated by color.

encodings.line: Coefficient trajectories and dashed reference lines
encodings.text: Panel titles, shared legend, and reference labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Three warm-start vision tasks compare FIRE with standard and Muon coefficients. Curves visibly overlap closely, but the caption does not state seeds or band semantics and no exact difference or test is printed.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix B.3 follows the recurrence-coefficient discussion and tests the practical choice of standard coefficients; Figure 6 covers iteration count and Figure 5 the main proxy ablation. No public plot source was found.
design_strengths: The matched three-task design isolates one algorithmic choice.
Shared axes and references make near-overlap visible without repeating legends.
design_weaknesses: “Newton Schulz” is not hyphenated consistently.
Visual overlap alone does not establish the surrounding “not significant” claim; bands are undefined and reference semantics are not captioned.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a matched multi-task coefficient comparison with common references, paired with an exact difference/uncertainty summary for near-overlapping curves.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Train accuracy of continual visual learning experiment. Warm-start setting (a), Continual setting (b), and Class-incremental setting (c).

color.semantic_mapping: The Figure 2 vision method palette is reused for FIRE, baselines, and Base across the training curves.

encodings.line: Training trajectories and repeated reset dips
encodings.text: Row labels, panel titles, shared legend, and axes

figures.data_and_statistics: Train accuracy is shown for the same warm-start, continual, and class-incremental protocols as Figure 2; class-incremental has two panels because CIFAR-10 is outside that protocol. No uncertainty, seed aggregation or exact values are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 8 is the train-side companion to Figure 2’s test curves, making repeated intervention drops visible. It connects Appendix B.4 to the visual-learning claim but adds a descriptive training-dynamics view rather than a new estimand.
design_strengths: Row-aligned protocol structure supports direct comparison with Figure 2.
Reset dips make intervention dynamics visible without another diagram.
design_weaknesses: Eight panels and eleven hues are difficult to decode at page size.
The caption does not explain why train accuracy or dips matter; no bands or seed information are shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a train-side companion grid to explain intervention dynamics behind a test curve, while explicitly annotating reset events and keeping the shared legend readable.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Wall-Clock Time and GPU memory footprint of FIRE and baseline methods

tables.uncertainty: Appendix B.1 says values are averaged over ten trials, but the table gives no dispersion and does not identify mean versus median.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three method rows compare wall-clock reset overhead and GPU memory: Shrink Perturb 0.002 sec/27 MB, FIRE 0.06 sec/55 MB, and DASH 69 sec/2834 MB. These are cost values rather than end-to-end training-time denominators.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix B.1 bounds the practical cost of the methods and qualifies the proxy/efficiency story in Figure 5; no main-body table duplicates this cost view.
design_strengths: Time and memory are on one compact decision surface with explicit units.
The minimal rule system is easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: Ten-trial context and TITAN RTX/Ryzen/64 GB hardware are outside the caption.
No workload denominator, dispersion, or total training cost is shown.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair intervention time and memory in a small cost table, with hardware, workload, aggregation and variance attached to the caption or note.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Detailed settings in continual visual learning.

tables.uncertainty: Configuration table; no measurement uncertainty applies.
tables.data_and_statistics: Seven parameter/value rows specify Adam, learning rate 1e−3, Warmup, gradient clipping 0.5, batch size 256, 100 epochs per chunk, and no augmentation.
tables.evidence_relation: Supports Figure 2 and Figure 8 reproduction; Tables 7–9 later list selected method-specific values.
design_strengths: Compact parameter/value grammar is readable and machine-translatable.
Citations remain inside the value cell when needed.
design_weaknesses: Three-seed count and detailed warmup/chunk schedule are outside the table.
Learning-rate and clipping units are implicit in the parameter names.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a two-column inventory for stable defaults, then put schedule semantics and replication metadata in an adjacent note.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Detailed settings in continual pretraining of LLMs.

tables.uncertainty: Configuration table; no measurement uncertainty applies.
tables.data_and_statistics: Seven parameter/value rows specify AdamW, weight decay 1e−1, learning rate 6e−4, minimum learning rate 6e−5, warmup + linearly decaying schedule, clipping 1.0, and batch size 480.
tables.evidence_relation: Configures Figure 3’s checkpoint facets; Table 10 lists checkpoint-specific values and surrounding prose gives the two-phase schedule.
design_strengths: Explicit minimum learning rate and schedule prevent ambiguity in the basic optimizer setup.
Visual hierarchy matches Table 2.
design_weaknesses: GPT-0.1B, data mixture, phase lengths and three-seed replication are external.
The table does not expose the exact phase transition steps.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Hyperparameters used in the ALE environment with DQN algorithm.

tables.uncertainty: Configuration table; no measurement uncertainty applies.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fourteen rows enumerate optimizer/epsilon controls, gamma, replay buffer 10^6, minibatch 32, initial collection 20,000, ten training iterations, 250K environment steps per iteration, replay ratio 1, target update period 2,000, and Huber loss.
tables.evidence_relation: Fixes the implementation context for the DQN row of Figure 4; the DQN README additionally documents its vectorized four-environment reproduction difference.
design_strengths: Covers optimizer, replay, exploration, target-update and loss controls in one inventory.
One-column parameter/value grammar keeps the operational context auditable.
design_weaknesses: Five-seed replication, environment count and intervention timing are outside.
Long parameter names make the narrow table dense.
tables.reusable_pattern: Enumerate optimizer, replay, exploration and target-update controls together, with workload and seed metadata adjacent.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Hyperparameters used in HumanoidBench environments with SimBa.

tables.uncertainty: Configuration table; no measurement uncertainty applies.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fourteen rows specify AdamW, learning rate 1e−4, weight decay 0.01, actor hidden dim 128/one block, critic hidden dim 512/two blocks, gamma 0.99, clipped double-Q, replay buffer 10^6, minibatch 256, initial collection 5,000, replay ratio 2, and tau 0.005.
tables.evidence_relation: Provides continuous-control reproduction context for Figure 4(b), complementing Table 4’s ALE/DQN settings.
design_strengths: Actor/critic capacity and target-update semantics are explicit.
The two-column layout stays compact.
design_weaknesses: Task-specific environment details and five-seed replication are external.
The table does not indicate which values were tuned versus adopted.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use paired algorithm-family parameter tables with explicit network dimensions and target-update controls, and state tuning provenance next to them.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Hyperparameter search space for all experiments.

tables.uncertainty: Search-space inventory; it contains no performance estimate or uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four grouped experiment blocks (Warm-Starting, Continual Learning, Class-Incremental Learning, and continual GPT-0.1B pretraining) use Experiment, Method, Hyperparameters, and Search Space columns. The rendered table contains 28 data rows.
tables.evidence_relation: Bridges the default settings in Tables 2–5 to selected per-dataset/checkpoint values in Tables 7–10 and bounds tuning behind Figures 2–5.
design_strengths: Multirow groups make protocol-specific ranges easy to locate.
The four-column header makes ranges explicit and keeps search metadata separate from outcomes.
design_weaknesses: The body is wide and small; no search-budget, objective, split or selection-rule column appears.
Repeated method rows increase scanning cost and do not establish tuning provenance.
tables.reusable_pattern: Separate search ranges from selected configurations in grouped wide tables, while adding budget and selection criterion when tuning is central.

tables.evidence_relation: Connects Table 6 search ranges to Figure 2(a), Figure 5(a), and Figure 7’s warm-start comparisons.
design_strengths: Dataset–method specificity preserves per-benchmark tuning.
Repeated dataset groups make the 24-value matrix auditable.
design_weaknesses: Generic Value hides parameter name and units.

design_strengths: Parallel structure with Table 7 supports protocol-to-protocol comparison.
Dataset groups retain the benchmark boundary.
design_weaknesses: Generic Value column obscures parameter semantics; no tuning budget, selection metric or seed count is shown.

tables.uncertainty: Configuration table; no measurement uncertainty applies.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes constrained stability–plasticity geometry; Figure 2 carries visual protocols; Figure 3 tests LLM checkpoint sensitivity; Figure 4 extends to discrete/continuous RL; Figure 5 separates iteration choice from curvature/DfI/SFE proxies. Appendix Figures 6–8 explain iteration dynamics, coefficient robustness and train-side recovery, while Tables 1–10 cover cost, defaults, RL controls, search ranges and selected values.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Objects use Figure/Table n: captions with descriptive titles. Figure titles are generally bold and setup/comparison oriented; Figures 2–4 define protocols or intervention markers but no shaded-band semantics. Figure 5 error bars and Figures 6–8 scale/uncertainty details are not defined. Table captions are short title-only labels, with seeds, hardware, schedules and parameter semantics in surrounding prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Parameter | Value is stable for defaults and RL controls; search and selected tables use Experiment | Method | Hyperparameters | Search Space, Dataset | Method | Value, or Method | CKPT | Value. The generic Value column hides parameter identity in Tables 7–10, and no table combines performance, cost, failure and uncertainty.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: SFE defines stability and DfI defines plasticity; Figure 5(b) visualizes proxy separation, Figures 2–4 show downstream behavior, and Figure 6 shows iterative movement. Figure 7 tests coefficient choice and Figure 8 exposes train dynamics. The chain is coherent, but rank/dormancy consequences are not directly measured and proxy bars have no exact companion table.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main figures carry conceptual, cross-domain and ablation evidence. Appendix B adds cost, iteration, coefficient and train-accuracy diagnostics; Appendix C gives implementation detail; Appendix D describes baselines; Appendix E gives seeds, hyperparameters, search ranges and selected settings. The appendix extends the same claim families.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Native manuscript/caption/table typography is highly consistent, while compact raster plot labels create a smaller secondary system and Figure 1 uses a separate diagram style. At 200 dpi plots are readable, but 6–8 pt legends and eleven-method palettes are small.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Red FIRE is a useful recurring anchor and blue often denotes Base or an alternative variant; other method colors are local. Figures 2 and 8 reuse the vision palette, while Figures 3 and 4 use local legends. The system is not grayscale-safe and tables carry no color semantics.

most_reusable_patterns: A compact conceptual geometry diagram maps an optimization constraint to the intersection of competing properties.
Protocol-aligned small multiples with shared axes and a common method legend expose warm-start, continual and class-incremental regimes.
A mechanism-oriented ablation places iteration choice, curvature/plasticity/stability proxies and a full-reset reference together.
Appendix tables separate defaults, search spaces and selected per-dataset/checkpoint values from outcome figures.
Intervention-aligned RL facets use one visible event marker across tasks and control families.
highest_value_objects: Figure 2 is the main visual-learning evidence surface, exposing protocol differences and test-curve behavior.
Figure 3 is the strongest checkpoint-sensitivity view for continual LLM pretraining.
Figure 4 is the broadest domain-transfer object, aligning six post-intervention RL trajectories.
Figure 5 is the key mechanism/ablation bridge from NS iterations to SFE/DfI/curvature proxies.
Table 1 and Figure 6 together bound reset cost and iteration dynamics.
failure_patterns: Shaded ribbons and Figure 5(b) error bars are not defined despite reported three- or five-seed runs.
Main outcome figures lack exact endpoint/result tables, denominators and statistical tests, so numerical auditability is limited.
Eleven-method palettes are not grayscale-safe and local legends force method-color relearning across domains.
Tables 7–10 use a generic Value header that hides parameter identity; search budget, selection criterion and tuning provenance remain in prose.

The public repository has matching rendered assets for Figures 2–4 but no plotting scripts, data exports, paper TeX or table generators; the automatic inventory row understates partial visual-source evidence.
Newton–Schulz recurrence coefficients differ between the Algorithm 1 discussion on p. 6 and Appendix B.3 on p. 24; Figure 5 also contains the Netwon-Schulz caption typo.
The theory is assumption-bound and its rank/dormancy consequences are not visually measured; the main visuals show DfI/SFE and behavior but not a direct neuron-activity or effective-rank diagnostic.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: A restrained ICLR serif layout uses one conceptual geometry figure, rasterized protocol-aligned small multiples and proxy/iteration diagnostics, plus compact appendix configuration tables to move from FIRE’s stability–plasticity objective to cross-domain behavior, while leaving uncertainty definitions, exact numeric result surfaces and source-generating code incomplete.
